title: Rest-frame annihilation lines of $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in 23,000 stacked galaxy clusters
html:
Abstract:Weakly interacting massive particle (WIMP) annihilation features were reported as a 43 GeV line in three Fermi-LAT galaxy clusters ($\mathtt{S}_3$), as triad $\{\gamma\gamma, \gamma Z,\gamma h\}$ lines from $\sim70$ GeV WIMPs in LAT data cross-correlated ($\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$) with western eROSITA X-rays, and as a nonad (combining three triads) of two cross-annihilating WIMPs in $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$. A blind scan of LAT 16.3-year data around 23,343 high-latitude clusters in their rest frames finds three triads, at 70 GeV ($2.8\sigma$ trial-corrected, henceforth), $72$ GeV ($1.3\sigma$; strengthening to $2.7\sigma$ if mass-fixed by $\mathtt{S}_3$, $4.0\sigma$ combined with $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ masked around the clusters, $5.7\sigma$ if also combined with $\mathtt{S}_3$), and 74-75 GeV: a triplet not only rare ($3.5\sigma$) but also forming a $\{70,74\}$ GeV nonad ($3.4\sigma$; strengthening to $4.0\sigma$, $4.6\sigma$, and $6.1\sigma$, respectively). The spectral features, robust in and out of the $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ region and $\mathtt{S}_3$ clusters, appear in all Galactic quadrants and only in the cluster rest frame (vanishing upon redshift rescaling or permutation), fade away from cluster centers, are absent from their surrounding stacked fields, and like $\mathtt{C}_{\mathtt{W}}$ indicate intrinsic few $10^{-19}$ cm$^3$ s$^{-1}$ cross sections (uncorrected) across samples. All features are largely explained by cross-annihilating $69.7^{+0.4}_{-1.0}$ and $74.5^{+1.1}_{-0.6}$ GeV WIMPs.
